rv.q: Bill Paterson as Adam Smith presides over this indispensable play with the relaxed air of a man who knows that his faith in the free market has been all too readily accepted.
It's vivacious and mischievous, yet often heavy-handed. And the screwy ending is completely misjudged.
Bruce Norris has the greater skill of skewering his targets with comic precision.

cn.t: Bruce Norris's ambitious three-hour picaresque fable earns praise as a mischievous theatrical extravaganza, with critics applauding its bold satirical take on capitalism and entrepreneurship across American history.
